content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I am a data scientist with six years in analytics and data science, and I am moving towards machine learning engineering. At Thistlebox, I build forecasting and churn workflows used by operations and retention teams, and I design experiments with product and growth colleagues. I am interested in applying this experience to AI systems that help merchants get support quickly and without friction.

My recent work includes a six-week-ahead demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM and engineered calendar, price and menu-position features. Run as a scheduled notebook job, it writes forecasts to BigQuery for operations teams; WAPE fell from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also developed a weekly-scored XGBoost churn model and built a sequential-testing calculator in Python and Streamlit, writing the app and its Dockerfile while the data platform team handled Cloud Run deployment. These projects have given me practical experience with feature engineering, data workflows and collaboration across teams.

I work with Python, BigQuery and dbt, and in 2025 began adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage. My production experience is primarily with scheduled and batch workflows rather than model APIs, and my PyTorch experience is from a learning project. I would bring a strong statistical foundation, practical machine-learning experience and a deliberate focus on developing my production engineering practices. Quillstone’s emphasis on ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes is particularly appealing to me.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Customer Operations AI team.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately tailored to the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. It uses credible quantified outcomes, including the reduction in WAPE from 23% to 14% and the estimated 9% reduction in food waste. It also accurately explains the candidate’s level of production ownership rather than overstating experience. The letter’s main weakness is that the third paragraph foregrounds several limitations, which may make the candidate appear less ready for the role than necessary. It could present the transferable evidence more positively while remaining fully truthful.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings and plain text, includes relevant terms such as Python, BigQuery, dbt, pytest, feature engineering, data workflows, LightGBM, XGBoost, Streamlit, Docker, and Cloud Run, and avoids formatting that would interfere with parsing. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because several core ad terms are absent or not directly connected to the candidate’s experience, including GCP, orchestration, data ingestion pipelines, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, AI products, chat assistants, and RAG. These are primarily candidate-experience gaps, not defects in the letter. The document does, however, have truthful supporting material for explicitly naming GCP through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s emphasis on practical machine learning, feature engineering, Python, experimentation, scheduled data workflows, testing, and cross-functional collaboration. It also connects credibly to Quillstone’s interest in reducing friction for merchants and mentions ownership, teamwork, and learning from mistakes. However, the candidate’s background does not demonstrate several must-have requirements: four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML systems to production, chat assistants or RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, or the named MLOps tools. The candidate has related but narrower experience: scheduled notebook workflows, batch scoring in BigQuery, dbt, GCP-based tooling, and initial pytest adoption. The MSc Statistics and BSc Mathematics do not directly match a degree in machine learning, computer science, or an engineering field, although they are quantitatively relevant. The role is office-first in Hamburg while the candidate’s stated preference is remote; the letter appropriately does not misrepresent this, but it remains a practical application consideration.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, replace the limitation-heavy sequence beginning “My production experience is primarily with scheduled and batch workflows rather than model APIs...” with a more constructive, evidence-led description. For example: “My production experience so far has focused on scheduled and batch ML workflows: Vertex AI Workbench notebooks produce forecasts for operations, and weekly churn scoring runs in BigQuery. I have also begun applying production engineering practices by adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage.” This preserves the important limitation without making the paragraph lead with what the candidate lacks.

CRITICAL: In the second or third paragraph, explicitly name the supported GCP experience. Change “I work with Python, BigQuery and dbt” to “I work with Python and GCP-based data workflows, including BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, alongside dbt.” This is supported by the candidate’s portfolio and makes the cloud-provider requirement easier for ATS and recruiters to identify. Do not imply broader GCP infrastructure expertise.

MINOR: In the opening paragraph, change “I am interested in applying this experience to AI systems that help merchants get support quickly and without friction” to a more specific transferable-value statement, such as “I am interested in applying this experience to reliable AI systems that help merchants get support quickly and without friction, bringing a strong foundation in feature engineering, model evaluation, experimentation, and production data workflows.” This connects the candidate’s actual strengths more directly to the advertised AI systems work.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, replace “I would bring a strong statistical foundation, practical machine-learning experience and a deliberate focus on developing my production engineering practices” with “I would bring a strong statistical foundation, practical machine-learning experience, and hands-on experience building, evaluating, testing, and operating scheduled ML workflows.” This is more concrete and avoids framing the candidate primarily as someone who still needs to develop.

content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I am a data scientist with six years in analytics and data science, and I am moving towards machine learning engineering. At Thistlebox, I build forecasting and churn workflows used by operations and retention teams, and I design experiments with product and growth colleagues. I am interested in applying this experience to reliable AI systems that help merchants get support quickly and without friction, bringing a strong foundation in feature engineering, model evaluation, experimentation, and production data workflows.

My recent work includes a six-week-ahead demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM and engineered calendar, price and menu-position features. Run as a scheduled notebook job, it writes forecasts to BigQuery for operations teams; WAPE fell from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also developed a weekly-scored XGBoost churn model and built a sequential-testing calculator in Python and Streamlit, writing the app and its Dockerfile while the data platform team handled Cloud Run deployment. These projects have given me practical experience with feature engineering, data workflows and collaboration across teams.

I work with Python and GCP-based data workflows, including BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, alongside dbt, and in 2025 began adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage. My production experience so far has focused on scheduled and batch ML workflows: Vertex AI Workbench notebooks produce forecasts for operations, and weekly churn scoring runs in BigQuery. My PyTorch experience is from a learning project. I would bring a strong statistical foundation, practical machine-learning experience, and hands-on experience building, evaluating, testing, and operating scheduled ML workflows. Quillstone’s emphasis on ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes is particularly appealing to me.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Customer Operations AI team.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately candid about the candidate’s current level of production engineering experience. It uses concrete evidence, including the WAPE improvement from 23% to 14%, estimated food-waste reduction, weekly churn scoring, 40 annual experiments, and approximately 60% pytest coverage. The explanation that the candidate has batch and scheduled-workflow experience rather than API-based model serving is especially credible. The main content limitation is that it spends more space describing existing analytics workflows than explicitly translating them into the Customer Support AI team’s needs, such as support operations, data-processing pipelines, model evaluation, and cross-functional product integration. The degree and relevant academic background are also absent from the letter.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in its plain-text structure, standard headings-free letter format, readable paragraphs, and use of relevant terms including Python, feature engineering, model evaluation, experimentation, GCP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, pytest, Docker, Cloud Run, and scheduled ML workflows. AI screening probability is moderate to low for this particular role because the letter does not contain supported evidence for several high-priority terms: chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation, language models, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLOps, or named orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, or Airflow. These are substantive experience gaps rather than keyword problems, so they should not be added. The letter could nevertheless improve parsing and alignment by explicitly naming the candidate’s MSc Statistics, scheduled notebook orchestration, dbt Cloud scheduling, and data-pipeline-related work where accurately supported.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate aligns well with Python, GCP-based data workflows, feature engineering, model evaluation, experimentation, and operating scheduled or batch machine-learning workflows. The strongest evidence is the forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench writing to BigQuery, the XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery, and the tested Streamlit application packaged with Docker. The candidate’s MSc Statistics is a relevant quantitative foundation, although it is not a degree in machine learning, computer science, or engineering. The candidate does not show the required four years as a machine learning engineer shipping production ML systems; the experience is as a data scientist, with scheduled and batch workflows rather than independently served models. The candidate also lacks evidence of chat assistants or RAG, production model serving, monitoring, data versioning, and the specified MLOps tools. The letter appropriately does not claim these capabilities. The culture reference to ownership, teamwork, and learning is supported by the company information, but the office-first Hamburg arrangement conflicts with the candidate’s stated remote preference; the letter correctly does not misrepresent that preference.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the first paragraph, add the candidate’s academic credential and position it accurately, for example: “I hold an MSc in Statistics with a strong foundation in modelling uncertainty, experimentation and quantitative analysis.” Do not describe it as a machine-learning, computer-science, or engineering degree.

CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, make the supported orchestration and workflow details more explicit for ATS and recruiter review. Replace “I work with Python and GCP-based data workflows, including BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, alongside dbt” with wording such as: “I work with Python and GCP-based data workflows using BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, maintain dbt models, and use scheduled notebook and dbt Cloud workflows for recurring data and ML jobs.” This accurately reflects the candidate’s material without implying MLflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, or broader MLOps expertise.

MINOR: In the second paragraph, connect the transferable experience more directly to the advertised team without claiming support-AI experience. After the forecasting and churn examples, add a sentence such as: “Although my production experience has focused on forecasting, churn and experimentation rather than conversational AI, these projects developed my ability to turn messy business data into evaluated, repeatable workflows used by operational teams.”

MINOR: In the final paragraph, replace the broad phrase “building, evaluating, testing, and operating scheduled ML workflows” with the more precise “building, evaluating, testing, and operating scheduled and batch ML workflows.” This keeps the wording fully consistent with the candidate’s stated experience and avoids any possible implication of independent online model serving.

MINOR: In the closing paragraph, change “could contribute to the Customer Operations AI team” to “could contribute to the Customer Operations AI team through reliable data preparation, feature engineering, model evaluation, and scheduled ML workflows.” This uses supported job-related terminology while avoiding unsupported claims about assistants, RAG, or model serving.
